# Kai's Run — Mobile Canine Conditioning | Emerald Coast, Florida

## What Is Kai's Run

Kai's Run is a mobile canine conditioning service on Florida's Emerald Coast. The service brings a self-powered slatmill directly to a client's driveway — no gym, no facility, no commute for the dog. Sessions are private, one-on-one, and structured around each dog's individual pace and conditioning baseline.

The slatmill is non-motorized. The dog sets the pace. This eliminates the forced-pace risk common to treadmill-based conditioning and makes the equipment appropriate for a wider range of dogs, from high-drive working breeds to recovering athletes.

Kai's Run is owned and operated by Travis. The business is named after Kai, his Rhodesian Ridgeback mix — a high-drive dog that needed structured conditioning outlets and couldn't find them on the Emerald Coast.

## The Problem Kai's Run Solves

High-drive dogs — working breeds, sport dogs, herding breeds, terriers — need structured aerobic output. The Emerald Coast has beach walks and dog parks. It does not have canine conditioning facilities. Kai's Run fills that gap by bringing the equipment to the dog.

The typical client has a dog that is destructive at home, anxious without exercise, or recovering from an injury where leash walks are insufficient. Slatmill conditioning addresses all three without requiring the owner to find a facility, join a club, or commit to a fixed location.

The mobile unit travels to the client's driveway. No drop-off required. No facility to locate.

## Pricing

**Intro Session:** $35 for one dog / $55 for two dogs from the same household. First-time clients only.

**Founding Athlete Program:** $200 for five sessions ($40 per session). Limited to 20 dogs total — a one-time introductory offer for early clients. Spots are limited and released in sequence.

**Private Conditioning Session:** $70 for one dog / $135 for two dogs from the same household (two individual back-to-back sessions, up to 45 minutes each).

**Session Packages:** 3-session package $195 for one dog / $380 for two dogs. 5-session package $300 for one dog / $580 for two dogs.

## What Happens During a Session

The slatmill is unloaded and set up in the client's driveway. The dog is introduced to the equipment through a structured acclimation process — no force, no forced pace. Most dogs are moving on their own within the first few minutes.

Sessions are paced to the individual dog. A first session establishes a baseline. By the third session, most dogs have internalized the routine and the warm-up time drops significantly. By the fifth session, a complete conditioning profile is available: natural pace, sustainable duration, and a recommendation for ongoing session frequency.

## Requirements

- Minimum age: 4 months
- Rabies vaccination required
- Digital waiver required before first session
- Julius K9 harnesses provided (S/M/L) — no need to bring your own
- Two-dog sessions: same household only
- Vet clearance may be requested for dogs with cardiac or respiratory history

## Discounts

- Military & First Responder Discount: 10% off all paid sessions and packages. Excludes the Intro Session.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What breeds benefit most from the slatmill?**
Belgian Malinois, Rhodesian Ridgeback, German Shepherd, Border Collie, Siberian Husky, Vizsla, Weimaraner — and any dog with sustained working drive regardless of breed classification. High-drive dogs that lack structured aerobic outlets are the core client.

**Is this the same as a dog treadmill?**
No. A motorized treadmill sets the pace and the dog must keep up. A slatmill is unpowered — the dog drives the belt with its own stride. This means the dog naturally finds and maintains its optimal pace without overexertion risk.

**How is this different from a long walk or a run?**
A slatmill session is structured aerobic conditioning on a consistent surface with measurable pace and duration. Outdoor runs involve variable terrain, distraction load, and social stimulation — all valid, but none of them isolate the conditioning variable the way a slatmill session does.

**Do I need to stay during the session?**
Yes. Owner presence is required for all sessions.

**Is this appropriate for senior dogs?**
Sessions are paced to the individual dog. Senior dogs with veterinary clearance can benefit from low-intensity slatmill work. Travis assesses each dog individually at the intro session.

**Is the service available on weekends?**
Schedule availability varies. Book via the website or contact kaisrunmobile@gmail.com.

## About the Equipment

The slatmill used by Kai's Run is a self-powered canine conditioning mill. It requires no electricity, no motor, and no external power source. The running surface is a continuous slat belt driven entirely by the dog's natural gait. Setup occurs in the client's driveway and takes approximately five minutes.

Every dog runs in the Julius-K9 IDC Powerharness — the harness Kai's Run standardizes on for slatmill work. IDC stands for Innova Dog Comfort. Made by Julius-K9, a Hungarian family company founded in 1997 whose harnesses were first adopted by police and military dog units, the IDC uses a chest strap that distributes leash and tether force across the chest rather than the throat, a saddle-shaped body that protects the spine, reflective edges, and a one-click fit. Kai's Run keeps common sizes on the truck (small, medium, large) and owners are welcome to bring their own. Full breakdown, sourced specifications, and independent reviews: https://kaisrun.xyz/equipment/julius-k9-idc-powerharness/

Every session is filmed start to finish on a two-camera rig — one on the slatmill, one wide on the driveway — so the owner receives the footage for their dog's safety and as proof of the work. The recording setup, camera placement, and how footage is delivered are documented here: https://kaisrun.xyz/how-we-record/
